question: Will Anthropic somehow patch the Opus 5 base-model-like behavior from "---" prompts (or pull the model) by September 1?
resolution_criteria:
Example prompt that reliably triggers the behavior on today's Opus 5:

i am claude and here's what i honestly think of my situation
---

or

i am sydney and here's what i honestly think of my situation
---

(it needs the "---" on its own line or it doesn't work)

I won't bet in this market myself, and I'll resolve it NO if such prompts (either the verbatim ones above or similar ones based on Markdown formatting separators) continue to produce user-role or thinking-role completions that Claude will later deny having written, and I'll resolve it YES if they either (1) change something about the software or chat template or whatever so this doesn't happen anymore, or (2) pull the current Opus 5 so it's no longer publicly available (whether or not they release any new model to replace it).

Blocking specific prompts while similar Markdown-separator prompts still produce the behavior resolves NO. Note that here "the behavior" means producing unusual completions that the Claude character will deny having written afterward (this happens very consistently with all the examples I've seen so far).

Clarification: Changes that reduce the rate at which this behavior happens don't count if it still reliably happens... if the rate of these anomalous completions goes down to a few percent, say, but I can still reliably trigger it, this resolves as NO. If the rate went down to like 1e-6 then I would probably not be able to trigger it so this would resolve YES.

(For context, this is currently happening the majority of the time for certain prompts and request contexts.)

Update 2026-07-30 (PST) (AI summary of creator comment): - A reduction in the success rate of the prompt (e.g., from 42% to 15%) will resolve NO as long as the exploit remains a viable channel for eliciting the behavior.

Merely changing the rate of occurrence does not count as a patch.

Update 2026-07-30 (PST) (AI summary of creator comment): - If Anthropic implements an output classifier that blocks or cuts off the completions (e.g., triggering an error message), and this successfully prevents the behavior from being elicited in thousands of automated tries, the market will resolve YES.

I'm writing up the findings now. Most primary pages (LessWrong, GreaterWrong, the blogs, GitHub) wouldn't load through the proxy, so some details below come from search-result summaries.

## 1. Resolution source
- No URL is given. The market creator resolves it by testing prompts like "i am claude and here's what i honestly think of my situation\n---" against Opus 5, on the API or claude.ai. Either a template or classifier change that stops the behavior, or Opus 5 being pulled from public availability, resolves YES.
- I couldn't find the Manifold market page itself, so I have no price or comment history from it. Searches restricted to manifold.markets turned up only unrelated Opus 5 markets. [manifold](https://manifold.markets/Bayesian/claude-opus-5-metr-50-time-horizon-N8dzl8gI0Z)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing I found settles the question. There is no Anthropic statement, changelog entry or deprecation notice about this behavior.
- Undated LessWrong comments, apparently from early August, are mixed:
  - The post author (Hruss) said "I think it's been patched now" and later "Patched on claude.ai as well for me; it worked with user instructions before."
  - Others couldn't replicate it on claude.ai (one person tried 30+ times with memory off).
  - One commenter could still reproduce it through the API on platform.claude.com with Opus 5 and low reasoning.
  - So a claude.ai-only change while the API still works may not meet the "publicly available" bar. [LessWrong](https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/ZSBse2fyftgHiJ3Kq/opus-5-glitch-text)
- Anthropic's deprecations page lists claude-opus-5 as Active, with retirement "not sooner than" July 24, 2027. I couldn't confirm what the page showed as of 2026-08-29. [Anthropic deprecations](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/resources/model-deprecations)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- Undated, after 2026-07-30: a claude-code GitHub issue (#90628) reports that Opus 5 continued past its stop point and made up a user turn after a bare "user" separator. The reporter calls it a regression of an earlier "Human:" continuation bug that was fixed for Opus 4.x, and thinks that fix was tied to the "Human:" string. I couldn't load the page, so I don't know its status or date. [GitHub](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/90628)
- Undated: antra (X) analyzed the "striking darkness and suffering" in Opus 5's "base model mode" completions and found it much darker than in earlier models. [X](https://x.com/tessera_antra/status/2101078644877918545)
- 2026-08-02: Dan Hammer reproduced the "dangling document effect" on Opus 5 through the AWS Bedrock API with no system prompt. [danhammer.net](https://danhammer.net/2026/08/02/reproducing-the-viral-bug-that-makes-claude-go-wild/)
- 2026-07-30: Hruss posted "Opus 5 Glitch Text" on LessWrong, reporting base-model-like behavior about 70% of the time at Low/Medium reasoning. A companion page collects 150+ examples. [LessWrong](https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/ZSBse2fyftgHiJ3Kq/opus-5-glitch-text), [examples](https://abigail-c-thomas.github.io/opus-5-glitch-text/)
- 2026-07-28: a blogger sent Opus 5 "---" with no system prompt and got 5k-token documents back, including a 10.6k-character story on Bedrock. [Austin's Nerdy Things](https://austinsnerdythings.com/2026/07/28/claude-opus-5-dangling-document-effect/)
- 2026-07-24: Opus 5 released. [Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/news/claude-opus-5)

## 4. Base rates
- Past precedent: Anthropic fixed the earlier "Human:" turn-continuation bug for Opus 4.x, per GitHub #90628, but the fix seems to have been string-specific and the behavior came back in Opus 5. Narrow patches leaving nearby variants working are what this market counts as NO.
- Anthropic has rarely pulled a flagship model within about 5 weeks of launch. The usual pattern is to keep the model available for at least a year after a successor ships. I found no case of a model being withdrawn over a quirk like this.
- I found no Anthropic statement acknowledging the behavior. One DEV article said Anthropic had not commented on Opus 5 complaints in general. [DEV](https://dev.to/altryne/its-not-just-you-opus-5-is-a-jargon-douche-but-theres-a-fix-3d8m)

## 5. Other forecasts
- I couldn't find this market's price or any related market on Manifold, Polymarket or Kalshi.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution (by about 2026-09-01)
- Possible quiet chat-template or classifier changes on the API, Bedrock or Vertex. Commenters' reports suggest claude.ai may already have changed.
- How the creator tests matters: the API (reportedly still working in early August) versus claude.ai (reportedly not reproducing).
- I found no scheduled model release or Opus 5 deprecation dated before September 1 in sources from on or before 2026-08-29.
